new: vāta-pūrṇa-koṣṭha-tvakka: tvakka is read as 'skin' (tvac extended); alternative 'the abdomen and skin full of wind'. new: The object drawn out from the heart is not named; the neuter singular endings suggest a piece (or the heart itself) is meant, but this is not stated. ciṭiciṭāyat is onomatopoeic (crackling, a denominative participle); indra-dhanus = Indra's bow, i.e. rainbow; the compound is read as 'crackling or rainbow-coloured' because of the following vā.
